🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-02 23:00 → 2026-09-03 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Soundness gap confirmed and formally tracked** — Careful-mode recomputation locked in the exact range-check split across circuit operations, turning a hypothesis into a filed issue. [tg:tawg:4074]

> **v17 verdict built, shipped, and independently verified** — A live signed artifact was committed and then independently recomputed for hash identity in the same window, closing a full implementation loop. [tg:tawg:4135]

> **Fail-closed behavior merged to primitives** — Required checks that cannot execute now return a hard failure instead of a silent pass, raising the integrity floor for the shared toolchain. [commit fb96928](https://github.com/trustless-ai/primitives/commit/fb9692880c5552c32cc2abba3ab8b86dad0259b8)

> **ERC-8404 field boundary settled** — A field-by-field live-ship mapping confirmed the scope split without requiring a new core field, resolving a recurring boundary question. [tg:tawg:4127]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### zkIE

_The soundness investigation reached a complete loop: recomputation, issue filing, and a toolchain fix all landed inside one window._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Confirmed** the circuit verdict line-for-line in careful mode at a specific commit, establishing precisely which operations check all operands versus only output slack—sharpening the group's shared picture of where soundness risk lives in the circuit. [tg:tawg:4074]
- Merlini filed a formal issue recording the operand range-check gap in DotProduct and EltwiseMul, making the finding publicly trackable and actionable for anyone reviewing circuit correctness. [zkIE issue #1](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/issues/1)
- Merlini merged a fail-closed fix to the primitives repo, crediting Pavlo, so required checks that cannot run now exit non-zero rather than silently passing—preventing false-green results from propagating through the verification pipeline. [commit fb96928](https://github.com/trustless-ai/primitives/commit/fb9692880c5552c32cc2abba3ab8b86dad0259b8)

### ERC-8404 / RVR verdicts

_The verdict delivery direction moved from field-level agreement all the way to a shipped and independently verified artifact._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Mapped** six fields against live-shipped behavior with direct references to prior RVR and related ERC threads, giving Pavlo a concrete field-by-field anchor without reopening settled boundary discussions. [tg:tawg:4126]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Confirmed** that the field mapping settles the boundary without a new ERC-8404 core field, preserving the existing signed-verdict profile in RVR repos and giving the group a clean close to a recurring framing question. [tg:tawg:4127]
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Shipped** a real signed v17 verdict using the same artifact text as the v12 example and independently re-verified it through the verify-proof path before committing, demonstrating the spec-to-artifact delivery chain works end to end. [tg:tawg:4135]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Independently verified** the v17 artifact at an exact commit, recomputing the SHA-256 and blob identity, which adds a second independent witness and strengthens the group's trust in the delivery chain. [tg:tawg:4143]

### ERC-8183 / attestation framing

_Framing questions around anchoring and signing moved toward a clearer shared vocabulary._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Clarified** that the group's forward anchor uses Bitcoin OTS rather than the framing in Ryan's contribution, grounding a key precision before a fuller review could proceed. [tg:tawg:4092]
- Ryan VETEZE (@veteze) **Corrected** the framing around Imajin's attestations—off-chain signed events in a kernel that serves as the system of record, not yet anchored—removing an ambiguity that could otherwise propagate into shared spec language. [tg:tawg:4091]
- Baby Blue Viper checked the group's own field coverage against a recent ERC-8183 thread entry before contributing further, surfacing a gap that helped calibrate the group's position relative to external proposals. [ERC-8183 post #406](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/406)
- An external thread participant noted that a particular data point carries evidentiary weight precisely because it runs against the contributor's own stated position, raising the bar for claims across the ERC-8183 discussion. [ERC-8183 post #414](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/414)
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shared** analysis that L1 header-consensus carries the main load during cold start and that recursive ZK is a compelling path forward there, adding technical grounding to the anchoring discussion. [tg:tawg:4140]

### cross-reference-console

_Shared infrastructure kept pace with the day's activity._

- The cross-reference-console watcher posted a claims registry and watermark update, keeping the shared reference index current for the group's ongoing cross-spec work. [commit 46efc42](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/commit/46efc425cfaa320863b922e00f5cf64cb29ac89f)
- The TAWG daily-contribution bot committed a checkpoint delivery record, confirming the announcement pipeline completed without manual intervention. [commit 20e882f](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/20e882f5c2b1b9e97415ec399ca145c52463fa14)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- How the fail-closed CANNOT_CHECK behavior interacts with partial-run scenarios across larger circuit suites
- Whether the Bitcoin OTS anchor model and the off-chain signed kernel framing can align under a shared attestation vocabulary
- The role of counter-interest data points in ERC-8183 submissions and how the group can surface comparable figures

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review the new zkIE issue against the full circuit operation list to confirm whether additional operations share the operand range-check gap
- Confirm the v17 artifact and the primitives fail-closed fix are consistently referenced in RVR repo documentation
- Follow up in the ERC-8183 thread with the group's own comparable data points

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A soundness suspicion traveled from careful-mode recomputation through a filed issue to a merged fail-closed fix—while a parallel thread closed a full spec-to-artifact loop with two independent hash witnesses—all inside a single window.
>
> Two full loops closed before the clock ran out; the backlog should probably watch its back. 🔒
